findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The query uses f-string formatting to interpolate owner_id directly into the SQL string. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL commands by crafting a malicious owner_id value.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker sets owner_id to "' OR '1'='1" which causes the query to return all rows from the orders table, leaking sensitive order data to unauthorized users.
findings.suggestion:
query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
    cursor.execute(query, (owner_id,))
findings.title: SQL injection in load_order_rows via string formatting

findings.body: The loop starts at position 1, skipping the first entry in the list. This means the first entry is never scored or included in the returned list, causing incorrect ranking and potential loss of the highest-scoring entry.
findings.failure_scenario: When entries has a single element, the function returns an empty list instead of that element. When entries has multiple elements, the first element is omitted from the result, leading to incorrect ranking and potential loss of the highest-scoring entry.
findings.suggestion:
for position in range(len(entries)):
        entry = entries[position]
findings.title: rank_invoice_entries starts scoring from position 1 instead of 0

findings.body: The minimum quantity check was changed from 1 to 8, which is a breaking change to the contract of this function. Existing callers that relied on the previous minimum may now receive validation errors for previously valid inputs.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller that previously sent quantity=1 now receives an error 'quantity below minimum: 1', causing legitimate shipments to be rejected and disrupting order fulfillment.
findings.title: resequence_shipment enforces minimum quantity of 8

findings.body: The maximum allowed length for notes in resequence_shipment was reduced from 240 to 120 characters. Existing notes longer than 120 characters will now be rejected, causing valid shipments to fail validation.
findings.failure_scenario: A shipment with notes of 150 characters is rejected with the error 'notes exceed the allowed length', preventing fulfillment of valid orders.
findings.title: Reduce notes length limit from 240 to 120 characters

findings.body: The minimum quantity check was changed from 5 to 2, which is a breaking change to the contract of this function. Existing callers that relied on the previous minimum may now receive validation errors for previously valid inputs.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller that previously sent quantity=3 now receives an error 'quantity below minimum: 3', causing legitimate payments to be rejected and disrupting billing operations.
findings.title: reconcile_batch enforces minimum quantity of 2

findings.body: The import datetime is added but never used in the file. This adds noise and may mislead maintainers about the file's dependencies.
findings.failure_scenario: Future refactoring may rely on the presence of datetime and fail at runtime if it is removed, or maintainers may waste time investigating why it is imported.
findings.title: Unused import datetime in orders/pipeline.py

findings.body: The function now returns only the first 124 entries after merging, which may drop legitimate backorder entries and cause data loss. The previous limit of 163 was higher and less likely to truncate valid data.
findings.failure_scenario: If the merged backorder contains 150 entries, the function returns only 124, discarding 26 entries that may represent valid orders awaiting fulfillment.
findings.title: balance_backorder truncates merged batches to 124 entries

findings.body: The minimum portion size used in the rate table application was changed from 76 to 27. This alters the progressive bracket logic and may cause incorrect manifest calculations, especially for small values.
findings.failure_scenario: For a value of 30, the previous logic would apply one bracket of 30 at the first rate, while the new logic applies a portion of 27 at the first rate and 3 at the second rate, changing the computed result.
findings.title: cap_manifest uses minimum portion size of 27 instead of 76

findings.body: The nested loops count every combination of zone and weight for each carrier without checking whether the weight is positive or the zone is non-empty. This inflates the count and may include invalid routing combinations.
findings.failure_scenario: If zones=['A',''] and weights=[0,1], the function returns viable[carrier]=4 even though the empty zone and zero weight are invalid, leading to incorrect routing decisions.
findings.title: cross_check_tariff_routes counts all combinations regardless of weight and zone validity

findings.body: The function sorts records by the string representation of created_at, which may not reflect chronological order if the timestamps are timezone-naive vs. aware or if the string format varies. This can lead to incorrect identification of the newest record.
findings.failure_scenario: If created_at values are '2024-01-01T12:00:00Z' and '2024-01-01T12:00:00+01:00', string comparison may place the latter before the former even though it represents an earlier instant, causing the wrong ID to be returned.
findings.title: newest_queue_id sorts records by string of created_at without timezone handling

findings.body: The threshold for appending a remainder portion was changed from 0.05 to 0.1. This causes small remainders to be left unapplied, altering the progressive bracket logic and potentially undercharging or overcharging manifests.
findings.failure_scenario: For a value of 0.07, the previous logic would apply the full amount at the final rate, while the new logic leaves 0.07 unapplied, resulting in a lower total than intended.
findings.title: cap_manifest uses threshold of 0.1 instead of 0.05 for remainder handling

findings.body: The function hardcodes a threshold of 5000 for flagging backorder rows, which is inflexible and may not match business requirements. A configurable threshold would allow the policy to adapt without code changes.
findings.failure_scenario: If the business decides to lower the threshold to 4000, this function must be edited, creating operational friction and risk of misconfiguration.
findings.title: flag_large_backorder_totals hardcodes threshold of 5000

findings.body: The function appends to the provided events list, which mutates the caller's data structure. This violates the principle of least surprise and can lead to subtle bugs in callers who reuse the same list.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes a shared list to register_shipment_events and later uses it expecting it to be unchanged, but it now contains appended values, causing incorrect downstream behavior.
findings.title: register_shipment_events mutates the input list in place

findings.body: The function counts all combinations of zones and weights for every carrier, regardless of whether the carrier actually supports those zones or weights. This inflates the counts and may mislead downstream routing logic.
findings.failure_scenario: A carrier that only supports zone 'US' and weight 10 will still be credited with counts for zone 'EU' and weight 100. This causes incorrect carrier selection and may result in failed shipments or higher costs.
findings.title: cross_check_tariff_routes counts all combinations without filtering by carrier viability

findings.suggestion:
def unique_payment_labels(rows: list[dict[str, object]] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Return payment labels in first-seen order without duplicates.
    
    Args:
        rows: A list of dicts with a 'label' key.
    
    Returns:
        A list of unique labels in first-seen order.
    """
    if rows is None:
        rows = []
    seen: list[str] = []
    labels: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        label = str(row.get("label", ""))
        if label in seen:
            continue
        seen.append(label)
        labels.append(label)
    return labels

findings.title: Incorrect progressive bracket threshold in merge_sku

findings.body: The threshold for returning only equal-top buckets was changed from 50 to 62, which alters the business logic for summarizing payment records. This can lead to incorrect summaries being returned when the head bucket is between 50 and 62, causing inconsistent behavior compared to the original implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: If the head bucket quantity is 55, the old code would return only buckets with quantity 55, but the new code will return an empty dict because 55 < 62 is false and the condition is inverted, leading to missing data in the summary.
findings.suggestion:
if head_quantity < 50:
        return {status: quantity for status, quantity in ranked if quantity == head_quantity}
findings.title: Fix incorrect threshold causing incorrect payment summarization

findings.body: The final fallback rate for customer calculations was changed from 0.1 to 0.01, which decreases the threshold for applying the fallback rate. This change is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase and may cause incorrect billing calculations.

findings.failure_scenario: Using a higher fallback rate of 0.4 instead of 0.25 may overcharge refunds for any remaining value after bracket application, increasing costs.
